Lycanthropy is wolf-madness, in which the patient believes he is a wolf. Burton treats it as a species of madness elsewhere in the Anatomy.
French. It gave the English 'alamort': dejected, dispirited, half dead with gloom.
Burton parodies the pharmacological scale of degrees of heat and cold. That scale normally stopped at the fourth degree, so 'eight' is an exaggeration.
Priapismus is the medical term for a persistent, painful erection of the penis. Burton lists it as one of the diseases that Mercurialis's case reports show alongside melancholy.

Vertigo is the Latin medical term for giddiness or dizziness. It was already used in English in Burton's day. Here it is one of the conditions Burton lists, from Montanus's case reports, as occurring together with melancholy.
Ratio terms: superbipartiens tertias is 5:3 (a whole plus two thirds), and superbipartiens quintas is 7:5. The grammar is clipped and mock-technical.
